analysis.title: ECB: Changing Times?
key_insights: Citi sees a shift in ECB communication from the first pillar of its framework (inflation outlook) to the second and third (underlying inflation dynamics and policy transmission). It argues this justifies market expectations of a more moderate rate path.

Citi argues the shift shows the ECB reaction function has been unstable recently. In the September press conference the President focused almost exclusively on the first pillar and said the Council is not 'attaching great importance in the current circumstances to the neutral rate'.

In her 28 September European Parliament hearing, the President stressed the lack of evidence that higher energy prices feed into wages and the rise in long-term yields, which slow growth and reduce pass-through from an exogenous price shock.

Citi's baseline is unchanged: the Governing Council holds rates this week, probably hikes 25 bps in December, and possibly hikes again in March 2027. This is conditional on no further deterioration in the French sovereign bond market and no global financial tensions, for instance over confidence in AI investment.
Citi says its rate expectations are better described as a distribution than a modal forecast, given exogenous influences and two-way risk to energy prices from an unstable geopolitical situation.

Citi expects the ECB President may announce an early departure soon (Bloomberg, 30 Sep). This would let governments decide in one discussion on replacing three key Executive Board positions (President, chief economist, markets board member), and Isabel Schnabel is leaving in early January.

Citi expects the next President to be Pablo Hernandez de Cos or Klaas Knot, the two names most cited in the media (Bloomberg, 23 Oct). It expects their leadership to be more pronounced from the outset than that of previous Presidents.

Citi defines doves as central bankers who see inflation mainly as supply and demand. They are patient with exogenous shocks and weight the transmission and underlying-dynamics pillars more. It defines hawks as those who stress inflation expectations, are more backward-looking and weight the inflation-outlook pillar more.

Citi argues hawk or dove status cannot be read from a banker's inclination to hike or cut at a given time. It is better assessed by how often they refer to the output gap versus inflation expectations.
Citi expects the ECB reaction function to be more stable once a new President with a clearly articulated view of price formation takes over.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Citi's baseline is a hold this week, with the bar for further tightening higher because policy rates are at the upper end of the neutral range.
Citi's baseline, conditional on no further deterioration in French sovereign bonds and no global financial tensions.
A possible second hike under the same conditions. Citi frames its rate view as a distribution rather than a point forecast.

risk_factors: Further deterioration in the French sovereign bond market.
Global financial tensions, for instance over confidence in AI investment.
Two-way risk to energy prices from geopolitical instability.
Instability of the ECB reaction function and leadership turnover (President, chief economist, markets board member, possibly a fourth position).
geopolitical: Citi cites a still unstable global geopolitical situation creating two-way risk to energy prices.
Citi cites an idiosyncratic rise in sovereign spreads from a loss of confidence in French fiscal dynamics.

key_data_points.metric: Citi's expected ECB rate hike in December 2026
key_data_points.context: Baseline is a hold this week, a probable 25 bps hike in December and a possible hike in March 2027.
key_data_points.anchor: probably hike them by 25 bps in December, and possibly hike them again in March of next year

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: realised inflation and energy-driven price rises put inflation expectations at risk, so the ECB should keep hiking (a probable 25 bps in December and possibly March).
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: with rates at the upper end of the neutral range, there is no evidence of energy prices feeding into wages (no second-round effects) and long-term yields are rising, so the bar for more hikes is higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further deterioration in the French sovereign bond market, or global financial tensions such as over confidence in AI investment, would undermine the hike baseline.

theme_stances.key_argument: A change of emphasis from the inflation outlook to underlying inflation dynamics and policy transmission justifies expectations of a more moderate policy rate path.
theme_stances.evidence: justifies market expectations of a more moderate path for policy rates

theme_stances.key_argument: A new President with a clearly articulated view of price formation should make the reaction function more stable.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect the central bank reaction function to be relatively more stable
